notes: SNES PLAYER_NAME commands are represented explicitly as Android-style %S(index,0) placeholders for comparison only.
Android anchor intervals include following English-empty localization slots.
Very-high-confidence SNES-to-Android-English identity is not rejected merely because French wording is freely adapted.
When French or Android segmentation crosses individual anchors, preserve and review the complete local sequence block rather than forcing a per-ID translation.

units.source_display:
I'm Pecard, caretaker of
this lighthouse.
units.android_english_display:
I'm Pecard, caretaker of this lighthouse.
Not too many ships come by nowadays
with the seas so rough, but it sure is
pretty looking out at the ocean.
units.french_display: Je suis Picard, gardien de ce phare. Avec cette mer agitée, les bateaux ne passent guère plus, mais je reste à mon poste.
units.note: Android 2303-2306 is one contiguous lighthouse speech run. 2303 expands the SNES caretaker introduction and immediately precedes accepted 2304/2305.

units.source_display:
The power of the ancients
must have been incredible!
units.android_english_display: The power of the ancients must have been incredible! I'm betting there are even MORE unbelievable things buried under the continent!
units.french_display: La puissance des civilisations anciennes est impressionnante ! Je suis sûr que ce continent recèle bien des prodiges.
units.note: Android 2306 begins with the exact SNES ancients-power sentence and directly follows accepted 2305 in the same lighthouse run.

scenes.label: Waterfall fragmented opening and falling scream

units.note: Exact final falling scream at Android 3494, immediately after already accepted 3492/3493.

units.source_display:
I studied the power of
 Mana, which sustains
 eveything in this world.
units.android_english_display: I studied the power of Mana, which sustains everything in this world... That power is now slowly fading away.
units.french_display: Elle m'a tout appris de la force de Mana qui soutient notre monde. Celle-là même qui disparaît aujourd'hui...
units.note: Android 886/887 is the contiguous Jema/Luka-followers speech. 887 starts with the complete SNES sentence and adds the Android continuation.

units.android_english_display: This is the Kingdom of Pandora._
units.note: Android 237-240 is the exact ordered gate-guard run. 237 expands 'This is Pandora' to 'This is the Kingdom of Pandora' immediately before accepted 238-240.

units.source_display:
Odd things have been
happening ever since!
Grandma goes there...
units.android_english_display: Odd things have been happening lately! Even Grandma has been going there...
units.french_display: Ma grand-mère aussi est bizarre, elle qui est si énergique d'habitude...
units.note: Android 300/301 is the same two-part NPC speech; 301 closely matches the missing second SNES block and directly follows accepted 300.

scenes.label: Phanna and Dyluck exchange ordered gap

units.french_display: Oh... je vois. Mais je suis sûre qu'il va bien.
units.note: Exact Android-English line 305 fills the only gap between accepted 304 and 306 in the same conversation.

Android 1058 is the exact Phanna ellipsis and immediately precedes Android 1059 and the already aligned 1060-1068 scene. Android 1059 is semantically related to the following SNES line but remains layout-deferred because it resegments around PLAYER_NAME(1).

units.source_display:
KING:What a nightmare!
 The people in my country
 are acting like zombies!
units.android_english_display: King: What a nightmare! The people in my country are acting like zombies, and I have no idea when the empire might strike!
units.french_display: Roi : Je suis très inquiet. L'Empire pourrait attaquer à tout moment, et mes sujets sont comme des zombies !
units.note: Android 388 contains the complete SNES king nightmare/zombie sentence plus an Empire-warning expansion; it belongs to the same ordered court scene as 390-394.

units.source_display:
Let's forget we ever had
 this discussion. How
 absolutely impertinent!
units.android_english_display: No, let us forget we ever had this discussion! Never in all my days...!
units.french_display: Réflexion faite, je préfère que nous annulions tout ! Jamais je n'ai subi un tel affront !
units.note: Android 369 is the same cancellation/indignation line and immediately follows accepted 368 in the Elman scene.

units.source_display:
You did it, %S(0,0)!
Brightness is returning 
to normal everywhere!
units.android_english_display: You did it, %S(0,0)! Once again is cheer returning throughout the kingdom!
units.french_display: Roi : Bravo, %S(0,0) ! Notre royaume a retrouvé sa joie de vivre et son énergie !
units.note: Android 403 combines the two SNES text fragments around PLAYER_NAME(0): 'You did it, %S(0,0)!' and the kingdom returning to normal.

units.source_display:
I hope someday I can forge
 such a splendid sword!
units.android_english_display: I get tingles just looking at it. I hope someday I can forge such a splendid sword myself!
units.french_display:
Je ne pouvais pas la laisser dans un tel état !
Ah, j'espère que j'arriverai à en forger une aussi belle, un jour !
units.note: Android 566 contains the complete missing hope-to-forge-a-sword sentence and directly follows accepted 565.
SNES 'Separated from %S(1,0).' and Android '%S(1,0) leaves.' are the same party-removal event; Android 440 immediately follows accepted departure line 439.

units.android_english_display: Sprite: Hrmph. Now don’t you get in my way,_ Brother!_
units.french_display: Lutin : Ouais, ouais..._Mais t'as pas intérêt à me mettre des bâtons dans les roues,  mon gars !
units.note: Android 616/617 is the expanded sprite address ending in 'Brother!' immediately before accepted Android 618, which answers that address with the player reply at Android 618.
